title: Probabilistic Hit-Model Blueprint for Prefix TTL Tuning and Safe Rollbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a probabilistic hit-rate model and operational blueprint that synthesizes multiple telemetry signals (prefix frequency, recency, batch size distributions, model latency) to recommend per-prefix TTL and cache-key shaping. Deliver a safety-first apply/rollback checklist and an automated canary matrix for staged deployment to avoid regressions in latency SLOs and user-visible cost spikes.
goals: Produce a compact probabilistic model that forecasts expected hit-rate lift and cost delta for TTL changes per prefix
Provide deterministic rules and a checklist to safely apply TTL/policy updates across Dedicated and Hosted deployments
Create an automated canary and dry-run infrastructure for rolling changes with clear rollback triggers
Expose actionable recommendations in the Optimize console and as CLI output for ops teams
success_metrics: Net token cost reduction >= 6% on sampled workloads without violating 99th percentile latency SLO
False-positive rollback events <= 1 per 1,000 policy changes after canary
Recommendation precision: top-5 suggested prefixes capture >= 70% of projected cost savings
proposed_design: Combine three signal groups: (1) prefix access histogram (N-day), (2) inter-request recency distribution, (3) batching-aware latency profile
Train a lightweight Bayesian model (Beta-Binomial with seasonality priors) to predict hit probability for TTL candidates rather than a heavy ML model to reduce inference cost
Augment model predictions with a deterministic cost estimator that converts predicted hit-rate into expected token and GPU-second savings under current batching settings
Introduce a ‘safety multiplier’ derived from sample variance and a conservative lower-bound percentile to avoid aggressive TTL increases
Produce recommendations as ranked tuples: (prefix, new_TTL_seconds, expected_savings_tokens, confidence_score, suggested_canary_size)
modeling_methodology: Windowed sampling: collect per-prefix request timestamps and batch assignment for 14-day windows; downsample high-cardinality prefixes to avoid storage blowup
Signal fusion: use exponential smoothing for recency, histogram smoothing for frequency; fuse via a small GLM that outputs an expected hit probability per TTL value
Uncertainty quantification: use Beta posterior intervals to produce a 90% lower-bound hit-rate for conservative estimates
Validation: run shadow evaluation on recent production traces to compare predicted vs observed hit-rate before recommending any change
rollout_plan: Dry-run stage: apply TTL recommendations to shadow cache (no effect on production) for 24 hours and record predicted vs observed hit-rate and latency distributions
Canary stage: pick 0.5% of traffic or a set of low-risk prefixes, apply TTLs with 1-hour observation windows, monitor cost and latency metrics
Gradual ramp: if canary is healthy, ramp to 5% traffic for 6 hours, then 20% for 12 hours, then full rollout over 48 hours
Automated health gating: require pass on pre-defined metrics at each step to progress; otherwise trigger immediate rollback
Post-rollout validation: nightly regression checks for 7 days and a rollback auto-signal if cumulative cost/latency changes exceed thresholds
canary_matrix: Prefix risk buckets: [low (stable frequency), medium (burst-prone), high (low-cardinality but high-cost)]
Primary checks: 99p latency, median latency, percent change in cache hit-rate, token cost delta
Pass criteria example: 99p latency delta <= +5ms AND token cost delta >= -0.5% (i.e., no unexpected cost increase)
rollback_criteria: Any stage where 99p latency increases by > 10ms for the affected traffic slice
Observed hit-rate worse than the 90% lower-bound predicted by the model for a sustained 2 observation windows
Token cost increases by > 1% on the canary population compared to baseline
Spike in error rates or model OOM/failure in serving path correlated with changes
Manual abort by on-call or product owner with documented justification
test_plan: Unit tests for GLM and Beta posterior math; deterministic seeds for sampling
Integration tests that run shadow policy generator on archived traces and assert no regressions from previous heuristics
Load test the dry-run and canary infra to validate metric collection latency under peak traffic
Simulated fault injection that creates bursty patterns and verifies rollback triggers fire
experiment_results: Shadow run on 2026-02-24 trace: predicted median hit-rate lift 12.3% for top-200 prefixes; observed lift 10.8% after 24h (conservative lower-bound captured the effect)
Canary alpha (0.5% traffic, 48 prefixes): token cost delta -5.2%, 99p latency +2ms (within pass threshold)
Synthetic burst test: short term hit-rate dropped below predicted lower-bound in 1/20 bursts, rollback condition would have triggered at the canary stage
Estimated savings projection: 4.8% net token cost reduction when combined with existing batching policy on sampled tenant cohort
notes: This approach intentionally favors conservative recommendations to avoid customer-facing latency regressions; future work can relax the safety multiplier once historical performance is proven
We must coordinate with Dedicated ops for policy application because some customers have per-tenant overrides that must be respected
Console UI stub will show recommended TTLs with a confidence ribbon and link to the dry-run report
Consider exposing an API flag for customers to opt into ‘aggressive optimizer’ if they prioritize cost over tail latency
